questions.q: A script on the companion gets no replies addressed to it. The most common cause:
options: A bad CRC in the autopilot's replies
questions.explain: The route to its compid appears after the first packet from the target.

questions.q: The autopilot forwards a broadcast message (target_system = 0):
options: Only to the port with the GCS

questions.q: Why is UDP better than TCP for telemetry over 4G?
options: TCP holds fresh data behind stale
UDP encrypts the data at the protocol level
questions.explain: Head-of-line blocking: on loss, TCP retransmits stale data and holds back the fresh data.

questions.q: A vehicle with a 4G modem behind the carrier's NAT. How does the GCS connect to it?
options: Open a port on the modem
questions.explain: Incoming connections to a private IP are impossible.

questions.q: Two GCSs with sysid 255 on one network lead to:
options: Automatic selection of the primary GCS

questions.q: Disabling MAVLink forwarding through a port in ArduPilot 4.7+:
questions.explain: MAVn_OPTIONS bit 1 is the ArduPilot 4.7 name; in 4.6 and earlier it was SERIALn_OPTIONS bit 10 (and MAV_SYSID was called SYSID_THISMAV).

questions.q: What reproduces a bad network on Linux without a radio?
QGroundControl on a laptop lost the vehicle as soon as a script started. The configuration:
questions.fragment:
SITL: --out udp:127.0.0.1:14550
QGC: listening on UDP 14550
script.py: mavutil.mavlink_connection('udpin:0.0.0.0:14550')
options: The script and QGC listen on the same UDP port 14550: you need a second SITL output (14551) or a router
udpin in the script grabs sysid 255, and QGC drops the vehicle as foreign
QGC requires MAVLink 1 on port 14550, and pymavlink switched the whole SITL stream to MAVLink 2
SITL sends data only to the first client connected over TCP 5760
questions.explain: One UDP port, one listener; split the streams with a router or separate outputs.
